candidate: Current-v3 cost-quality routing result in Optimizing the Cost-Quality Tradeoff of Agentic Theorem Provers in Lean

published_claim.current_headline: 28.9% average cost decrease over fixed-step baseline while preserving performance
published_claim.version_scope: The current v3 headline is 28.9%; older v1 mirrors/search results still report 25.8%, so numeric claims must be version-qualified.
source_worker_related_claims: C601: 85-problem PutnamBench subset, seed-42 42/43 train-test split, 28.9% current-v3 cost decrease and 7.9% parity-cost accuracy improvement.
C602: the measured controller frontier is narrow; the oracle gap should not be read as evidence for untested richer action families.
C603: verifier-grounded trajectory features and separately modeled marginal action cost are the transferable mechanism, not the exact SFLOP proxy.

supports: Exact Putnam split file is committed and says Seed 42, Total 85, Train 42, Test 43.
Simulation engine, cost-quality policy, probability/cost feature machinery, Dockerfile, uv.lock, and pinned mathlib4 submodule are committed.
CostQualityPolicy scores real actions by p - lambda*c after an optional hot start; RunningAverageCostModel uses observed total_sflops.
proof_simulation explicitly replays pre-recorded proof attempts rather than invoking the prover online during policy sweeps.

reproducibility_gaps: The committed one-stage sweep config is an example config using example_problems_train_test_split.txt and scratch/results/... inputs; it is not an immutable paper-run Putnam config.
The config references models/onestage_logistic_train.json, but that generated trained model artifact is not committed at the inspected revision.

README paper commands reference some configs such as configs/proof_simulation/sweep_fixed_test.yaml that are absent at the inspected revision; the committed counterparts are under configs/proof_simulation/example/ where applicable.

The repository tree contains no committed paper results/ directory, per-seed summaries/trajectories, or the scratch/minified proof-attempt inputs required to rerun the exact policy sweep from preserved outputs.

Because the simulator draws from historical pre-recorded attempts, reproducing the policy computation is cheaper than regenerating proofs, but exact paper headline replay still requires the exact historical attempt corpus, trained router artifact, paper-run config, and output aggregation bundle.

No protocol-matched third-party reproduction of the 28.9% v3 headline was found in the public searches performed in this audit; the public GitHub repository showed zero forks at audit time, which is only weak negative evidence.
scope_corrections: Treat 28.9% as current-v3 primary-study evidence, not as independently reproduced.
Do not mix v1 25.8% / 7.8% / 59.9%-oracle numbers with v3 without explicit version qualification.

The official generic CostQualityPolicy supports more actions than a binary Attempt/Terminate abstraction, so claims about the evaluated binary control architecture must be tied to the paper experiment rather than generalized from this reusable policy class.
The experiment evaluates routing over a frozen historical attempt pool; it supports cost-aware allocation over those trajectories, not an end-to-end live proof-generation deployment replay.

Verified cost model consumes total_sflops and uses target-local then global running averages.
Verified simulation framework documentation states no actual proving is performed during replay simulation.
Verified exact dependency lock and pinned mathlib submodule exist.
Verified the referenced trained one-stage model artifact and top-level paper result outputs are absent from the inspected tree.

A protocol-matched independent rerun reconstructs the v3 cost-quality curve/headline.
